John Dewey on certainty

John Dewey (1859–1952) approaches certainty within Pragmatism. Inquiry reconstructs experience by forming hypotheses and testing consequences in a shared world. Democracy is a way of associated living and communicative problem-solving, not merely periodic voting. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets certainty most directly—useful for searches such as “john dewey quotes on certainty.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the John Dewey thinker page for biography and to the certainty theme for other voices on the same question.
